item.title: Las pérdidas aseguradas por catástrofes en el primer semestre, en su nivel más bajo desde 2020
item.description: Swiss Re Institute estima las pérdidas aseguradas por catástrofes naturales en el primer semestre de 2026 en 42.000 millones de dólares, el nivel más bajo desde el primer semestre de 2020 y un 16% inferior a la media decenal.

item.title: LMIC Launches ISI AI for Submission Ingestion, Achieving 98%+ Accuracy
item.description: Go-live advances trusted submission intake workflows for professional liability underwriting Toronto, Ontario and Los Angeles, California – August 25 – ISI announced that Lawyers’ Mutual Insurance Company (LMIC) has successfully integrated ISI AI into its submission processing workflow. With the ISI AI Submission Agent now in production, LMIC’s underwriting team can access more complete, organized submission information earlier in the review process. Since going live, ISI AI now creates 67% of LMIC’s new business quotes with a 98%+ extraction accuracy rate prior to human involvement.

item.title: Why Bootstrapped Businesses Are More Relevant Than Ever
item.description: The more common path is bootstrapped or self-funded: Start with an existing customer problem and get paid more than it costs to solve it. The path may take longer than the VC “go big or go home” approach, but many small companies scale into middle market businesses, and a few of the best find their way to market leadership, even in tech. For every VC-backed startup, there are hundreds of bootstrapped founders building profitable businesses without any outside investment.

item.title: Inside The Private-Market Divide: EquityZen’s Phil Haslett On AI, SaaS And Secondaries
item.description: Phil Haslett , who co-founded EquityZen and serves as its chief strategy officer, has had a front-row seat to the secondary market’s evolution. As startups stay private longer, the market for buying and selling shares in venture-backed companies before they go public has become increasingly active — and heated. EquityZen has been operating in that market since 2013.

item.title: Artemis London 2026: One week today. Register now if you want to attend the conference!

Artemis London 2026 will be our fifth in-person catastrophe bond and insurance-linked securities (ILS) market conference held in the City of London. item.title: Alternative reinsurance capital and ILS market growth forecast for 2027: Fitch
item.description: Fitch Ratings anticipates the growth of the alternative reinsurance capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS) market will continue in 2027, as risk-adjusted returns remain attractive to investors and sponsor demand for capacity remains high, despite the backdrop of reinsurance rate softening. “Fitch expects strong alternative reinsurance capital market growth and attractive risk-adjusted returns into 2027, with investor supply and sponsor demand well balanced,” the rating agency said. One of the big questions for the continued growth potential of ILS and alternative capital is how long discipline holds in the market and for now Fitch feels that all-important T&Cs in reinsurance are being sustained.

item.title: AM Best expects UK captive insurance regime to compare well with established domiciles
item.description: The UK insurance regulator’s recent consultation paper on a bespoke regulatory framework for single-parent insurance captives is expected to create a captive regime that compares well with other established captive domiciles, according to AM Best. The regime aims to enhance the UK’s insurance market proposition by creating an internationally competitive market for captives while maintaining appropriate safeguards through PRA and FCA oversight. AM Best expects the flexible capital requirement framework to give the UK a competitive proposition.

item.title: Fuse introduces AI-powered commercial insurance market intelligence via new Terminal platform
item.description: Fuse, an AI-powered market intelligence company focused on commercial insurance, has launched Fuse Terminal, a new workspace designed to give insurance professionals access to market intelligence, analysis and underlying filing information through a single interface. Terminal has been developed over two years to provide a more consolidated way of assessing the commercial insurance market. Fuse said one of Terminal’s principal features is ASK, an AI-powered analyst that allows users to submit questions in natural language from the platform’s command line.

item.title: Aviva adds terrorism cover as standard in digital SME policies, citing Pool Re scheme
item.description: British insurer Aviva has added terrorism cover as standard to selected digitally traded commercial products for eligible small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) customers in Great Britain, with the insurer citing the recent scheme launched by the UK’s terrorism reinsurer Pool Re as helping them expand coverage in this way. Terrorism reinsurance rates available through the scheme have been reduced by up to 90% for the majority of policies, helping minimise the cost of including the cover as part of the overall premium. It follows the launch of Pool Re’s SME Incentive Scheme, an initiative designed to make terrorism protection more accessible and simplify broker-client conversations for SMEs.

item.title: New Zealand Insurance Industry Failing to Meet Māori Needs, Market Watchdog Says
item.description: New Zealand’s insurance industry is failing to consistently meet the needs of Māori, with affordability barriers and difficulties insuring collectively owned land leaving them less likely to have cover, according to a study by the market watchdog. “Participants also raised concerns about valuation, replacement costs and whether insurance products adequately reflect actual risk and cultural and intergenerational value.” The FMA oversees New Zealand’s financial markets and has identified significant knowledge gaps in the insurance sector about the experiences of Māori consumers and providers. The Financial Markets Authority research published Tuesday in Wellington found that 17% of the more than 950 Māori who participated in the study experienced problems with insurance in the last two years, which is almost twice the rate found in a similar survey of the general population.

item.title: Europe’s Record Heat Is Splitting Stock Winners From Losers
item.description: Even as Europe’s heat wave finally breaks, money managers say they’re still coming to terms with how climate change will affect their portfolios. Pictet Asset Management’s Katie Self says her firm has been fielding calls from clients about the risks and opportunities posed by the extreme heat. Nuveen says Europe’s drought will soon start affecting corporate credit spreads.

item.title: China’s Hackers Use DeepSeek for Attacks, Researchers Say
item.description: Chinese hackers are ramping up attacks after integrating DeepSeek and other open-source artificial intelligence models into their operations, highlighting attackers’ ability to leverage basic AI tools to hit targets abroad. Researchers said it wasn’t always possible to identify the AI model they used, but in general DeepSeek’s offerings are popular with hackers in the country because of its high performance and ability to be customized. While other models produced in the country are more powerful – including Moonshot’s breakout Kimi K3 model – hackers are drawn to DeepSeek’s relatively lax cybersecurity barriers and low cost of running, researchers said.

item.title: Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific appoints Scott Munafò as China CEO
item.description: Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific has appointed Scott Munafò as China CEO, a Shanghai-based role, effective 1 September 2026. Rodrigo Jimenez, regional chief executive officer at Allianz Trade in Asia Pacific, welcomed the appointment. Munafò joined Allianz Trade within the Multinationals team in 2015 and has spent over ten years shaping commercial strategy across four distinct regions.

item.title: Chubb partners with BBVA
item.description: Chubb has partnered with BBVA to offer fully digital travel insurance to the bank’s customers in Germany. BBVA also offers travel-related benefits including cashback and no foreign exchange fees on card purchases. The partnership extends Chubb’s strategy of distributing travel insurance through financial institutions, airlines and travel platforms.

item.title: Solace Care raises €2.1 million
item.description: Stockholm-based Solace Care has raised €2.1 million in pre-seed funding to expand its digital legacy-planning and bereavement-support platform. Founded in January 2025, Solace Care offers services before and after a policyholder’s death. According to Solace Care, it surpassed 25,000 covered lives during its first year and currently serves Sweden, Finland and Norway.

item.title: ANV to acquire Car Care Plan
item.description: Insurance intermediary platform ANV Group Holdings has agreed to acquire UK-based vehicle warranty MGA Car Care Plan from AmTrust Financial Services. Founded in 1976, Car Care Plan provides vehicle warranties, asset protection products and after-sales administration to more than 30 automakers and over 2,500 dealers. The transaction also includes Car Care Plan’s overseas subsidiaries in the US, Europe, Turkey and China, as well as Dent Wizard Ventures, a UK provider of mobile bodywork, paint and alloy-wheel repair services.

item.title: Amazon’s New Order Confirmation Emails Seen Boosting Phishing Risk
item.description: In recent weeks, Amazon customers on TikTok and Reddit have also wondered why product names and images were replaced with labels such as “Household item” or “Essentials item” in order confirmation emails. “If anything, it increases risk.” Phishing attacks often mirror official emails and trick people into clicking on a bogus link that might contain malware or request login credentials. Vishwanath says Amazon’s new confirmation emails could encourage users to click on links without verifying who sent them.

I am confident that, together with the local management team, Scott will successfully drive our growth ambitions and deliver continued success in this important and fast-growing market.” Munafò added: “Allianz Trade has been part of China’s trade story for nearly two decades – built on the strength of our team, our partners, and our customers who have trusted us through every cycle.

item.title: Kentucky High Court Recalculates Employer Attorney Fees, Recovery in Subrogation
item.description: And an employer’s share of attorney fees must be deducted from the amount available from subrogation—not from the full settlement amount in a worker injury suit, the Kentucky Supreme Court decided in separate cases last week. The ALJ then subtracted the employer’s share of attorney fees in the suit against the vendor, leaving some $117,000 available for recovery in subrogation. Kentucky law bars injured workers from collecting duplicate benefits from the employer and a third party, and allows employers to seek recovery of benefits through subrogation.

item.title: Nuclear Verdicts Go Boom, Increase 40.7% in 2025
item.description: Verdicts like this against corporate defendants have come to be known as nuclear verdicts, and the total from 2025—a 40.7% increase over 2024—is the highest Marathon has seen since 2009. So-called “nuclear” verdicts did not subside in 2025. Product liability cases resulted in 29 nuclear verdicts totaling $12 billion in 2025.

item.title: Markets/Coverages: Classic Car Insurer OpenRoad Expands to 40 States
item.description: OpenRoad Insurance, a provider of specialized insurance for classic and collector vehicles and related coverages, said it is now licensed in 40 U.S. The latest states added to OpenRoad Insurance’s portfolio include: New York; New Hampshire; Vermont; North Carolina; and Delaware. “Reaching 80% of states in two years is a testament to the hard work of our product team,” said Richard Hutchinson, chief executive officer of OpenRoad Insurance.

item.title: Los Angeles Faces Days of 100F Heat as Southwest Fire Risk Grows
item.description: Los Angeles is bracing for a lengthy heat wave as the weather system that’s cooked Texas expands westward and begins stripping moisture from Southern California’s terrain. Heat alerts stretch from Santa Barbara along California’s central coast to the U.S.-Mexico border more than 200 miles (322 kilometers) southeast. Temperatures in downtown LA are forecast to approach 100F (38C) each day through Friday, according to the US National Weather Service.

item.title: NHTSA Eyeing 1 Million GM Pickups, SUVs Over Engine Failure Concerns
item.description: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Friday it has opened a probe into 997,743 General Motors pickup trucks and SUVs over concerns related to engine failure. GM issued a recall last year to address concerns related to engine failure in the impacted L87 unit. Related: Tesla Recalling 20,000 US Vehicles Over Excessively Bright Low-Beam Headlights The auto safety regulator said it received 499 complaints alleging engine failures despite the vehicles having undergone an earlier recall remedy.

item.title: Register: Risky Future AI Tools for Insurance BPO & Consulting ‘Demo Day’ on August 26
item.description: In partnership with Insurance Journal, Risky Future’s AI Tools for Insurance BPO & Consulting Demo Day will be held on Wednesday, August 26, beginning at 1pm ET. Insurance Journal’s Risky Future series is hosting the “ AI Tools for BPO & Consulting ” Demo Day, a series of free AI tool demonstrations designed exclusively for Carriers, MGAs, Retail Agencies and Operations Executives. Risky Future Demo Day events are the latest in a series of live online events in which experts share solution demos addressing the latest challenges facing the insurance industry.

item.title: Highest-Ever Ocean Temperature Measured as Super El Niño Forms
item.description: Scientists have recorded the highest temperature ever measured in the world’s oceans, as climate change combines with a powerful El Niño in the tropical Pacific. Copernicus expects the trend to continue, with ocean temperatures now being supercharged by El Niño. The August record is particularly worrying because global ocean temperatures are typically highest in March and April, after the Austral summer, Copernicus said.

item.title: Florida Example on How to Adapt as Coastal Cities Face Storms, Rising Sea Level
item.description: Recent research shows that a rise in sea level driven by humans has increased the frequency of extreme coastal flooding around the world. As climate change threatens communities, Florida is showing how to build to adapt. The goal is to better withstand rising waters, worsening storms, saltwater intrusion, heat heaves and other climate impacts.

item.title: Amazon Plans Drone Delivery Expansion to Nearly 500 U.S. Locales
item.description: Amazon said on Wednesday it will expand its drone delivery service to reach hundreds of U.S. Amazon currently delivers by drone from 11 locations, including Papillion, Nebraska, and Ruskin, Florida. Amazon said its broad rollout will extend its reach to about 500 locales.

item.title: Travelodge CEO Quits After Hotel Assault Spurs Security Concerns
item.description: Travelodge has faced scrutiny over its safety protocols after a woman was sexually assaulted by a man who was given a keycard to her room at its Maidenhead hotel. “We will also continue to engage proactively and constructively with government and the wider hospitality industry on the issue of safety and security.” Founded in 1985, Travelodge is one of Britain’s best-known budget hotel operators with 630 sites mainly in the UK and Ireland, as well as several in Spain. has stepped down, as the chain pledged to beef up its security measures after a female guest was sexually assaulted at one of its properties.

Specific to Ruby Re, we expect to be fully deployed this year.” RGA launched its first reinsurance sidecar vehicle Ruby Re back in December 2023 , with the vehicle set to be focused on underwriting U.S.

item.title: Hurricane Lala triggers Hawaii’s parametric coral reef insurance
item.description: The Nature Conservancy’s (TNC) Hawaiʻi parametric coral reef insurance policy will pay for damage assessment and reef repairs for the first time since it purchased the United States’ first such policy four years ago, following recent impacts from Hurricane Lala which brought dangerous flooding, strong winds and major power outages across the state. Moreover, the parametric policy is designed to provide rapid funding for assessing and repairing coral reef damage caused by hurricanes and severe tropical storms across the Hawaiian Islands According to The Nature Conservancy, Hurricane Lala is the first storm—with sustained winds of 65 knots within the covered area—to trigger the insurance policy. In 2022, WTW, alongside TNC, launched the parametric coral reef insurance concept, with global reinsurer Munich Re underwriting the risk for the Hawaiian coral reef parametric insurance arrangement.

item.title: Hurricane Lala triggers The Nature Conservancy’s US coral reef insurance policy for first time
item.description: The Nature Conservancy’s (TNC) Hawaiʻi coral reef insurance policy will pay for damage assessment and reef repairs for the first time since it purchased the US’s first such policy four years ago, following Hurricane Lala’s impacts this weekend, which brought dangerous flooding, strong winds and widespread power outages across the state. This weekend’s Hurricane Lala is the first storm to trigger the insurance policy, with sustained winds of 65 knots within the covered area. Active since 2022 , the parametric policy is designed to provide rapid funding for assessing and repairing coral reef damage caused by hurricanes and severe tropical storms across the Hawaiian Islands.

item.title: Guy Carpenter adds Jessica Ciak to Healthcare team
item.description: Guy Carpenter, a business of Marsh and a global risk and reinsurance specialist, has announced that Jessica Ciak has joined the firm’s Healthcare Segment as Senior Vice President, focusing on the US Medical Professional Liability sector. Ciak will be based in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and report to Martha Jacobs, Guy Carpenter’s Healthcare Segment Leader. Jessica brings the expertise, perspective, and leadership our clients need to manage rising severity trends, aggregation exposures, and reinsurance capacity pressures.” Ciak added: “I’m thrilled to be joining Guy Carpenter at this critical time for the medical professional liability market.

item.title: AM Best places At-Bay under review with positive implications amid Munich Re acquisition
item.description: Credit ratings agency AM Best has placed At-Bay Specialty Insurance Company (ABSIC) under review with positive implications following the recently announced acquisition of its parent company, At-Bay, Inc., by Munich Re for an enterprise value of USD 575 million. AM Best explained that the under review with positive implications status “reflects the potential financial and operational benefits that ABSIC may derive from being part of a significantly larger insurance organisation, which is of greater financial strength.” The ratings will remain under review pending completion of the transaction and AM Best’s evaluation of parental support, integration plans and the expected impact on ABSIC’s future business plans. After this, At-Bay will be overseen by Hartford Steam Boiler (HSB), part of Munich Re’s Global Specialty Insurance business.

item.title: Alfalfa Sprouts Linked to Food Poisoning in Minnesota and Wisconsin
item.description: Wisconsin investigators have identified another 18 cases of illness tied to alfalfa sprouts, Minnesota officials said. The illnesses are being linked to alfalfa sprouts produced by Everything Sprouts, a Minnesota grower, and sold under the Calco and Everything Sprouts brands to restaurants and grocery stores, Minnesota officials said. Minnesota health officials are warning consumers not to eat certain brands of alfalfa sprouts that have been tied to an unusual outbreak involving different disease-causing bacteria.

item.title: People Moves: TDI Names Kranes as Deputy Commissioner of Strategy and Performance
item.description: The Texas Department of Insurance (TDI) announced Michelle Kranes as deputy commissioner of the Strategy and Performance Division on August 17. Kranes will oversee the division that supports TDI’s strategic planning, performance and risk management, and process improvement through technology, automation, and business innovation. Kranes started her state career at the Texas Sunset Advisory Commission, where she evaluated state agencies and developed recommendations to enhance efficiency, accountability, and results.

item.title: AM Best Upgrades Credit Ratings of Arkansas’ Kinsale
item.description: AM Best has upgraded the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) to “a+” (Excellent) from “a” (Excellent) and affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A (Excellent) of Kinsale Insurance Company (Kinsale) based in Little Rock, Arkansas. These Credit Ratings (ratings) reflect Kinsale’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its strong operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM). Concurrently, AM Best has upgraded the Long-Term ICR to “bbb+” (Good) from “bbb” (Good) of Kinsale Capital Group.

item.title: Manulife launches CoverMe travel insurance app inside ChatGPT
item.description: Manulife has launched a ChatGPT app that allows Canadian travellers to receive personalised CoverMe travel insurance quotes. Once a quote is generated, they can continue to CoverMe.com, where the information provided in ChatGPT carries over to the purchase process. Users answer questions about their age, province of residence, destination, travel dates, and trip cost.

item.title: $5.5bn buyout: KKR-backed consortium to acquire Steadfast Group, with Amwins and Dragoneer
item.description: The post $5.5bn buyout: KKR-backed consortium to acquire Steadfast Group, with Amwins and Dragoneer appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Australian insurance broker Steadfast Group has agreed to a $5.5bn buyout by a consortium backed by investment firm KKR. Under the deal, specialty insurance distributor Amwins Group will acquire Steadfast’s underwriting agency business, while Dragoneer Investment Group will take control of its broking operations.

item.title: $1.6bn deal: RiverStone International takes on QBE legacy reserves
item.description: RiverStone International has entered into loss portfolio transfer reinsurance agreements with QBE Insurance, covering approximately $1.6bn of reserves. Paul Brockman, group chief executive officer of RiverStone International, welcomed the deal. The agreements expand the companies’ existing relationship and transfer responsibility for managing the legacy liabilities to RiverStone.
